question: What labelling requirements apply to Ayurveda Aahara products?
answer:
**India**



- Labelling of Ayurveda Aahara must comply with the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 and the specific labelling requirements set out in the Ayurveda Aahara Regulations. [1]

- The front of the pack must display the words “AYURVEDA AAHARA” in close proximity to the product name or brand and the logo prescribed in Schedule E, together with a prominent advisory warning “ONLY FOR DIETARY USE”. [2]

- The label must state that the product is not a substitute for a varied diet, include any known side‑effects, contraindications, drug or product interactions, and warn that it is for oral consumption only and not for parenteral use. [2]

- Every label must specify the intended purpose, the target consumer group, the recommended duration of use, and a storage warning that the product should be kept out of reach of children. [1] [2]



**Sources**



[1] [Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations 2022: original Gazette](https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf#page=16) | PDF page: 16 | https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28

[2] [Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations 2022: original Gazette](https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf#page=17) | PDF page: 17 | https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28

question: an I patent a traditional Ayurvedic formulation?
answer:
**India**



- A traditional Ayurvedic formulation is excluded from patentability under Section 3(p) of the Indian Patents Act because it is considered traditional knowledge. [5]

- Section 3(e) further bars patenting of a mere admixture of known ingredients that only aggregates the known properties of the components. [5]

- Guidelines for processing patent applications state that a formulation whose ingredients and therapeutic use are already disclosed in the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library lacks novelty and inventive step, and therefore is not patentable. [6]



**Sources**



[5] [Guidelines for Processing Patent Applications Relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material (2012)](https://ipindia.gov.in/frontend/pdf/patents/guidelines/Guidelines%20for%20Processing%20of%20Patent%20Applications%20relating%20to%20Traditional%20Knowledge%20and%20Biological%20Material%20-%202012.pdf#page=2) | PDF page: 2 | https://ipindia.gov.in/frontend/pdf/patents/guidelines/Guidelines%20for%20Processing%20of%20Patent%20Applications%20relating%20to%20Traditional%20Knowledge%20and%20Biological%20Material%20-%202012.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28
